domains.name: AI Strategy & Value Management
domains.definition: Able to set direction for AI and convert it into measurable institutional value.

domains.name: AI Demand & Solution Shaping
domains.definition: Able to find, qualify and shape AI opportunities into deliverable, adoptable solutions.

domains.name: Data & Knowledge Management
domains.definition: Able to supply trusted, governed data and knowledge to AI systems.

domains.name: AI Solution Engineering
domains.definition: Able to design, build, customize and validate AI solutions to a defined standard.

domains.name: AI Platform & Infrastructure
domains.definition: Able to provide and sustain the technical means to build and run AI.

domains.name: AI Operations & Reliability
domains.definition: Able to run AI in production dependably, observably and affordably.

domains.name: AI Governance, Risk, Security & Assurance
domains.definition: Able to direct, control, protect and evidence the trustworthy use of AI.

domains.name: AI People, Skills & Adoption
domains.definition: Able to build and sustain the human side of AI: who does it, who can, and who will.

capabilities.name: AI Vision & Strategy Definition
capabilities.definition: Able to establish and maintain a stated institutional position on AI and keep it current.

criteria.name: AI Ambition & Positioning
criteria.definition: Define what role AI plays in the institutional mandate and how far the organization intends to go.

criteria.name: AI Strategy Formulation & Refresh
criteria.definition: Produce and periodically revise an endorsed AI strategy with explicit scope and stated exclusions.

criteria.name: Strategic Alignment to Institutional Priorities
criteria.definition: Trace every AI objective to a corporate goal, sector strategy or country program.

criteria.name: AI Principles & Ethical Positioning
criteria.definition: Set the non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream AI decisions.

criteria.name: Horizon Scanning & Technology Foresight
criteria.definition: Track emerging AI capability and judge what it changes for the institution.

capabilities.name: AI Portfolio & Investment Management
capabilities.definition: Able to decide which AI work is funded, in what order, and when it stops.

criteria.name: AI Investment Case Development
criteria.definition: Build comparable business cases stating cost, benefit and risk on a common basis.

criteria.name: Portfolio Prioritization & Sequencing
criteria.definition: Rank and stage the AI portfolio against delivery capacity, risk appetite and dependency.

criteria.name: Funding & Budget Allocation
criteria.definition: Route funds to AI work through a mechanism that survives audit and annual planning.

criteria.name: Portfolio Balance & Exposure Management
criteria.definition: Keep the mix of experimental, scaling and production AI within stated tolerance.

criteria.name: Stage-Gate & Investment Review
criteria.definition: Decide continuation, pivot or termination at defined decision points on recorded criteria.

capabilities.name: Value Realization & Performance Reporting
capabilities.definition: Able to prove what AI actually delivered, to the standard a governing body accepts.

criteria.name: Benefit Definition & Baselining
criteria.definition: State expected benefit in measurable terms before build, with a recorded pre-intervention baseline.

criteria.name: Value Tracking & Attribution
criteria.definition: Measure realized benefit and attribute it defensibly to the AI intervention rather than to trend.

criteria.name: AI Performance Metrics & KPI Management
criteria.definition: Maintain the indicator set that describes AI performance institution-wide.

criteria.name: Executive & Board Reporting
criteria.definition: Report AI status, risk and value to governing bodies at their cadence and in their language.

criteria.name: Post-Implementation Review
criteria.definition: Assess delivered outcomes against the approved case and feed findings back into prioritization.

capabilities.name: AI Sourcing & Partner Strategy
capabilities.definition: Able to decide what is built, bought or partnered, and to stay able to change that decision.

criteria.name: Build / Buy / Partner Decisioning
criteria.definition: Choose the sourcing route per capability with recorded rationale and revisit triggers.

criteria.name: AI Vendor & Model Provider Evaluation
criteria.definition: Assess providers on capability, trustworthiness, transparency and cost of exit.

criteria.name: Contractual Safeguards & AI Clauses
criteria.definition: Secure rights covering data use, IP, indemnity, audit access and notification of model change.

criteria.name: Concentration & Exit Risk Management
criteria.definition: Limit dependence on any single provider and keep a tested, costed exit path.

criteria.name: Supplier Performance & Assurance Monitoring
criteria.definition: Monitor contracted providers against their obligations and assurance commitments for the life of the relationship.

capabilities.name: AI Ecosystem & Alliance Management
capabilities.definition: Able to hold external AI relationships that are not supplier contracts, and to stay operable when the ecosystem around them changes.
sources: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture

criteria.name: Partnership Portfolio Definition
criteria.definition: Decide which external relationships the institution needs in order to hold AI capability it will not build itself.

criteria.name: Research & Academic Collaboration
criteria.definition: Operate collaborations whose output is knowledge, method or evidence rather than a delivered system.

criteria.name: Peer & Multilateral Cooperation
criteria.definition: Exchange AI practice, assets and evidence with counterpart institutions under agreed terms.

criteria.name: Insourcing / Outsourcing Posture Management
criteria.definition: Set and periodically revisit which AI work is held internally and which is placed outside.

criteria.name: Ecosystem Dependency & Continuity Management
criteria.definition: Track aggregate dependency across the external AI ecosystem and stay able to operate when a member changes, merges or exits.

criteria.name: Partnership Value & Obligation Tracking
criteria.definition: Monitor what each relationship returns against what it obliges the institution to do.

capabilities.name: Use Case Discovery & Intake
capabilities.definition: Able to surface candidate AI work and admit it through one controlled front door.

criteria.name: Opportunity Identification & Ideation
criteria.definition: Actively generate candidate use cases from business need rather than waiting for requests.

criteria.name: Demand Intake & Triage
criteria.definition: Operate a single intake route that classifies and routes every AI request.

criteria.name: Use Case Registration & Classification
criteria.definition: Record each candidate against a common taxonomy before any build effort begins.

criteria.name: Duplicate & Reuse Screening
criteria.definition: Detect that a request is already solved, in flight, or satisfiable by an existing asset.

capabilities.name: AI Use-Case Feasibility & Qualification
capabilities.definition: Able to judge, before build, whether a use case is technically and operationally deliverable and worth doing.

criteria.name: Technical & Data Feasibility Assessment
criteria.definition: Judge whether the data, models and integration required actually exist and are obtainable.

criteria.name: Cost, Effort & Capacity Feasibility
criteria.definition: Estimate build and run cost, effort and the specialist capacity a use case would consume.

criteria.name: Operational & Adoption Feasibility
criteria.definition: Judge whether the receiving business area can absorb, operate and sustain the change.

criteria.name: Go / No-Go Determination
criteria.definition: Make and record a proceed decision with named accountability and stated conditions.

capabilities.name: AI Product Management
capabilities.definition: Able to own an AI capability as a product across its life, not as a project that ends.
sources: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture

criteria.name: AI Product Definition & Roadmapping
criteria.definition: Define the product, its users, its boundary and its forward path.

criteria.name: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria Management
criteria.definition: Express what good looks like precisely enough to be tested against.

criteria.name: User Research & Feedback Integration
criteria.definition: Learn from actual use and feed it back into the product.

criteria.name: Backlog & Release Planning
criteria.definition: Sequence work and commit to releases against capacity.

criteria.name: Product Performance Ownership
criteria.definition: Hold a named owner accountable for the product's outcomes in production.

capabilities.name: Business Process & Service Redesign
capabilities.definition: Able to change how work is actually done, not merely to add a model to an unchanged process.
sources: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture

criteria.name: Process Analysis & AI Fit Assessment
criteria.definition: Understand the current process well enough to know where AI changes it.

criteria.name: Target Process & Task Redesign
criteria.definition: Design the intended process, including what stops being done.

criteria.name: Human / Machine Task Allocation
criteria.definition: Decide explicitly which tasks move, which stay, and which become supervisory.

criteria.name: Control Point Redesign
criteria.definition: Relocate or rebuild the controls that the old process embedded in human steps.

criteria.name: Service Model & Service Level Redefinition
criteria.definition: Restate the service promise once AI changes what is deliverable.

criteria.name: Language Coverage & Service Equity
criteria.definition: Determine which languages an AI-delivered service must support, and at what measured quality, across the institution's countries.

capabilities.name: Human-AI Interaction & Oversight Design
capabilities.definition: Able to design the human's role in the system, rather than assert oversight in policy alone.

criteria.name: Autonomy & Interaction Pattern Determination
criteria.definition: Set and record, per system, the interaction pattern and how much an AI system or agent may do without human confirmation.

criteria.name: Human Oversight & Intervention Design
criteria.definition: Design the specific point, information and control through which a human can intervene.

criteria.name: Explanation & Disclosure Design
criteria.definition: Design what the system tells its user about what it is and how it reached an output.

criteria.name: Escalation & Handover Design
criteria.definition: Design the path by which work returns to a human, with sufficient context to act.

criteria.name: Oversight Competence & Workload Design
criteria.definition: Ensure the person assigned oversight has the time, information, training and authority to actually exercise it.

criteria.name: Accessible & Inclusive Interaction Design
criteria.definition: Design AI-delivered interaction to be usable with assistive technology and across literacy and channel constraints.

capabilities.name: AI Innovation & Incubation
capabilities.definition: Able to turn an untested AI idea into evidence, and evidence into either a funded product or a cheap, recorded stop.

criteria.name: Idea Capture & Innovation Sourcing
criteria.definition: Collect candidate AI ideas from staff, partners and technology watch outside the formal demand route.

criteria.name: Sandboxed Experimentation
criteria.definition: Run time-boxed experiments in an environment where failure is contained and permitted.

criteria.name: Innovation Portfolio & Scaling Decisions
criteria.definition: Hold the set of live experiments within capacity and decide which of them scale.

criteria.name: Experiment-to-Product Transition
criteria.definition: Move a proven experiment onto the funded delivery route, or record why it stops.

criteria.name: Controlled Failure & Learning Capture
criteria.definition: Permit experiments to fail and extract reusable learning from the failure.

capabilities.name: Data Governance & Stewardship for AI
capabilities.definition: Able to say who owns each data asset, who may use it, and under what conditions.

criteria.name: Data Ownership & Stewardship Assignment
criteria.definition: Name an accountable owner and an operating steward for each data asset used by AI.

criteria.name: Data Classification & Sensitivity Labeling
criteria.definition: Apply a consistent sensitivity classification that downstream controls can act on.

criteria.name: Data Access Policy & Entitlement Management
criteria.definition: Define and enforce who may access which data, for which purpose.

criteria.name: Data Retention & Records Management
criteria.definition: Apply retention and disposal rules to AI inputs, outputs and interaction records.

criteria.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Control
criteria.definition: Determine and enforce which jurisdictions the institution's data may be transferred to and processed in.

capabilities.name: Data Sourcing, Licensing & Provenance
capabilities.definition: Able to demonstrate lawful, documented origin for every dataset an AI system uses.

criteria.name: Data Acquisition & Onboarding
criteria.definition: Bring external and internal data into the estate through a controlled route.

criteria.name: Licensing & Permitted-Use Verification
criteria.definition: Confirm and record that intended AI use is permitted by the source's terms.

criteria.name: Provenance & Chain-of-Custody Recording
criteria.definition: Record where data came from and every transformation applied to it.

criteria.name: Consent & Purpose Limitation Management
criteria.definition: Track the basis on which data was collected and confine use to it.

criteria.name: Synthetic Data Generation & Control
criteria.definition: Produce and govern synthetic data, including disclosure of its synthetic nature.

capabilities.name: Data Quality & Preparation for AI
capabilities.definition: Able to make data fit for the specific AI purpose and to prove it was fit.

criteria.name: Data Profiling & Quality Assessment
criteria.definition: Measure completeness, accuracy, timeliness and consistency against stated thresholds.

criteria.name: Data Cleansing & Remediation
criteria.definition: Correct defects at source where possible, and record what was corrected downstream.

criteria.name: Representativeness & Bias Screening
criteria.definition: Test datasets for gaps and skews relative to the affected population.

criteria.name: Labeling & Annotation Management
criteria.definition: Produce, quality-check and version human and machine labels.

criteria.name: Dataset Versioning & Snapshotting
criteria.definition: Freeze and identify the exact dataset a model or evaluation used.

capabilities.name: Metadata, Lineage & Cataloging for AI
capabilities.definition: Able to find data, understand what it means, and trace where it went.

criteria.name: Data Catalog Management
criteria.definition: Maintain a searchable inventory of data assets with their attributes.

criteria.name: Business Glossary & Semantic Definition
criteria.definition: Hold one agreed definition per business term that data assets bind to.

criteria.name: Lineage Capture & Traceability
criteria.definition: Trace a model output back through transformations to source records.

criteria.name: Data Product Publication
criteria.definition: Publish curated, contracted datasets that consumers can depend on.

capabilities.name: Knowledge Corpus & Content Management
capabilities.definition: Able to curate the document and content estate that grounded AI depends on.

criteria.name: Corpus Definition & Curation
criteria.definition: Decide what belongs in a knowledge corpus and what is deliberately excluded.

criteria.name: Content Ingestion & Normalization
criteria.definition: Bring heterogeneous content into a consistent, machine-usable form.

criteria.name: Content Segmentation Design
criteria.definition: Choose and apply segmentation that preserves meaning and citability.

criteria.name: Corpus Freshness & Refresh Management
criteria.definition: Keep the corpus current and know how stale any part of it is.

criteria.name: Authoritative Source Designation
criteria.definition: Declare which source wins when two documents disagree.

capabilities.name: Knowledge Access & Retrieval
capabilities.definition: Able to return the right knowledge to the right requester, with its provenance intact.

criteria.name: Retrieval Service Provision
criteria.definition: Provide governed retrieval over institutional content — by meaning, by term, or both — as a reusable service.

criteria.name: Access-Trimmed Retrieval Enforcement
criteria.definition: Enforce, at retrieval time, the entitlements determined in 3.1.3, so a requester sees only what they may see.

criteria.name: Retrieval Quality Evaluation & Tuning
criteria.definition: Measure and improve retrieval precision and recall against a known set.

criteria.name: Multi-Source Federation & Ranking
criteria.definition: Retrieve across several repositories and rank the combined result coherently.

criteria.name: Citation, Grounding & Traceability
criteria.definition: Return every answer with the source it rests on, resolvable by the reader.

capabilities.name: Derived Representation Management
capabilities.definition: Able to manage derived representations of data as governed assets in their own right.

criteria.name: Feature Engineering & Store Management
criteria.definition: Produce, share and reuse engineered features under version control.

criteria.name: Embedding Model Selection & Versioning
criteria.definition: Choose embedding models deliberately and record which version produced which index.

criteria.name: Index Lifecycle & Re-embedding
criteria.definition: Rebuild and migrate indexes when content or embedding models change.

criteria.name: Derived Representation Governance
criteria.definition: Apply access, retention and residency controls to vector representations.

capabilities.name: AI Architecture Management & Solution Governance
capabilities.definition: Able to set, steward and enforce the architecture that AI solutions are built to.

criteria.name: Solution Pattern Selection
criteria.definition: Choose the architecture building block that realizes the required capability.

criteria.name: Reference Architecture Compliance
criteria.definition: Build to published reference architectures and detect deviation.

criteria.name: Architecture Decision Recording
criteria.definition: Record significant decisions with alternatives and consequences.

criteria.name: Non-Functional Requirement Design
criteria.definition: Design explicitly for latency, cost, availability, and degradation behavior.

criteria.name: Architecture Review & Dispensation
criteria.definition: Review designs and grant time-boxed exceptions with recorded conditions.

criteria.name: ABB & Pattern Stewardship
criteria.definition: Define, version and retire the institution's logical building blocks and the patterns that compose them.

criteria.name: Solution Conformance Certification
criteria.definition: Certify that a concrete solution conforms to the building blocks and controls it claims, and record the deviations.

capabilities.name: Model Selection, Customization & Tuning
capabilities.definition: Able to choose and adapt models on evidence, and to record what was done.

criteria.name: Model Selection for Use Case
criteria.definition: Select a model from within the cleared set against task-specific criteria and evidence.

criteria.name: Fine-Tuning & Adaptation
criteria.definition: Adapt models to institutional context under controlled, repeatable procedure.

criteria.name: Model Training & Experimentation
criteria.definition: Run and track experiments so results are reproducible.

criteria.name: Model Documentation & Disclosure Production
criteria.definition: Produce model cards covering intended use, limits, data and evaluation results.

criteria.name: Model Versioning & Registration
criteria.definition: Register every model version as an identifiable, ownable asset.

capabilities.name: Prompt & Context Engineering
capabilities.definition: Able to treat prompts and context assembly as versioned, tested engineering artifacts.

criteria.name: Prompt Design & Templating
criteria.definition: Design prompts as reusable, parameterized templates rather than embedded strings.

criteria.name: Prompt Versioning & Registry
criteria.definition: Version, review and register prompts as controlled artifacts.

criteria.name: Context Assembly & Window Management
criteria.definition: Assemble context deliberately and manage what is included, ordered and dropped.

criteria.name: Grounding Strategy Design
criteria.definition: Decide what the model is permitted to answer from, and enforce it.

criteria.name: Prompt & Context Boundary Design
criteria.definition: Construct prompt and context boundaries that constrain what untrusted content can instruct.

capabilities.name: Agent & Workflow Orchestration Design
capabilities.definition: Able to design what an agent may pursue, how it plans, and where it must stop.

criteria.name: Agent Specification & Goal Definition
criteria.definition: State an agent's objective, scope and prohibited actions before it is built.

criteria.name: Task Decomposition & Planning Design
criteria.definition: Design how an agent breaks work down and selects its next step.

criteria.name: Multi-Agent Coordination Design
criteria.definition: Design how agents delegate, communicate and resolve conflict.

criteria.name: Agent Memory & State Design
criteria.definition: Design what an agent retains, for how long, and who else can see it.

criteria.name: Guardrail & Constraint Design
criteria.definition: Encode hard limits an agent cannot argue its way past.

criteria.name: Termination & Loop Control Design
criteria.definition: Design stopping conditions, budgets and loop detection.

capabilities.name: Integration & Tool Enablement
capabilities.definition: Able to give AI systems safe, governed reach into institutional systems.

criteria.name: API & System Integration Design
criteria.definition: Design integration to institutional systems with contracts and error semantics.

criteria.name: Tool & Function Definition
criteria.definition: Define the callable actions exposed to a model, with typed inputs and stated effects.

criteria.name: Capability Exposure to AI Clients
criteria.definition: Expose institutional capability to AI clients through the prevailing open tool-interface standard.

criteria.name: Identity Propagation & Delegated Access
criteria.definition: Carry the acting user's identity through to the system of record.

criteria.name: Legacy & Core System Adaptation
criteria.definition: Reach systems that were never designed to be called by an AI client.

capabilities.name: AI Evaluation & Testing
capabilities.definition: Able to state, before release, what the system does and does not do reliably.

criteria.name: Evaluation Criteria & Metric Definition
criteria.definition: Define the metrics that constitute acceptable performance for this use case.

criteria.name: Golden Dataset & Test Set Management
criteria.definition: Build and maintain representative evaluation sets with known-correct answers.

criteria.name: Automated Evaluation Harness Operation
criteria.definition: Run evaluations repeatably as part of the delivery pipeline.

criteria.name: Human Review & Expert Evaluation
criteria.definition: Obtain qualified human judgement where automated metrics are insufficient.

criteria.name: Pre-Deployment Acceptance Testing
criteria.definition: Test against acceptance criteria and record the result as release evidence.

capabilities.name: AI Release & Change Management
capabilities.definition: Able to move AI change into production under control and to reverse it.

criteria.name: Build & Continuous Integration
criteria.definition: Build AI artifacts through an automated, auditable pipeline.

criteria.name: Promotion & Environment Progression
criteria.definition: Move artifacts through environments under defined entry and exit criteria.

criteria.name: Change Approval & Release Authorization
criteria.definition: Authorise AI change through a route proportionate to its risk tier.

criteria.name: Rollback & Release Reversal
criteria.definition: Return a deployed AI system to a previously accepted release.

criteria.name: Release Documentation & Evidence Capture
criteria.definition: Capture at release the evidence that later assurance work will need.

capabilities.name: AI Platform Service Provisioning
capabilities.definition: Able to offer AI platform services as a governed, supported institutional service.
sources: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI

criteria.name: Platform Service Catalog Management
criteria.definition: Publish what AI platform services exist, their terms and how to obtain them.

criteria.name: Landing Zone & Baseline Provisioning
criteria.definition: Provision AI environments from a compliant baseline rather than by hand.

criteria.name: Platform Configuration & Policy Enforcement
criteria.definition: Enforce configuration standards technically, not by instruction.

criteria.name: Platform Service Level Commitment
criteria.definition: Commit to and meet service levels for the shared AI platform services the institution offers.

criteria.name: Platform Upgrade & Deprecation Management
criteria.definition: Move consumers across platform versions without stranding them.

capabilities.name: Model Access & Traffic Management
capabilities.definition: Able to control which models the institution may call, through one governed path.
sources: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI

criteria.name: Model Clearance & Approved Model List
criteria.definition: Assess candidate models against institutional criteria, record the clearance decision and its conditions, and maintain the approved list.

criteria.name: Model Traffic Control & Routing
criteria.definition: Route all model traffic through a controlled point that can observe and enforce.

criteria.name: Quota, Throttling & Rate Management
criteria.definition: Allocate and enforce consumption limits per consumer.

criteria.name: Model Provider Credential Management
criteria.definition: Issue, rotate and revoke the credentials used to reach model providers and platform services. Agent identity is 7.4.4.

criteria.name: Model Version Availability & Provider Change Control
criteria.definition: Control which model versions remain reachable and absorb provider-side version change without breaking consumers.

capabilities.name: AI Environment & Workspace Management
capabilities.definition: Able to give teams isolated places to work without weakening controls.
sources: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI

criteria.name: Experimentation Environment Provision
criteria.definition: Provide safe environments for experimentation with clear data rules.

criteria.name: Workspace Tenancy & Isolation
criteria.definition: Define and enforce the tenancy and isolation topology between team workspaces.

criteria.name: Network & Private Connectivity Control
criteria.definition: Control network reachability of AI services and keep traffic private where required.

criteria.name: Environment Data Segregation
criteria.definition: Prevent production data from reaching environments not cleared for it.

capabilities.name: AI Compute & Capacity Management
capabilities.definition: Able to secure and allocate the compute that AI work requires.
sources: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI

criteria.name: Compute Provisioning & Scheduling
criteria.definition: Make compute available to workloads on a predictable basis.

criteria.name: Capacity Planning & Forecasting
criteria.definition: Forecast demand far enough ahead to secure supply.

criteria.name: Accelerator & Quota Allocation
criteria.definition: Allocate scarce accelerator capacity against portfolio priority.

criteria.name: Workload Placement & Residency Enforcement
criteria.definition: Place workloads in locations that enforce the transfer and residency decisions taken in 3.1.5.

criteria.name: Edge & Disconnected Operation
criteria.definition: Run AI where connectivity, latency or residency prevents central serving, including fully offline.

capabilities.name: Tool & Connector Catalog Management
capabilities.definition: Able to control what actions AI systems can reach, as a governed inventory.

criteria.name: Tool & Connector Catalog Management
criteria.definition: Maintain the inventory of actions and connectors available to AI systems.

criteria.name: Tool Source Registration & Approval
criteria.definition: Register and approve any source of callable tools before an AI client may reach it.

criteria.name: Tool Permission & Scope Governance
criteria.definition: Set and enforce the scope each tool grants, at least privilege.

criteria.name: Third-Party Tool Vetting
criteria.definition: Assess externally supplied tools and connectors before admission.

criteria.name: Tool Version & Deprecation Control
criteria.definition: Manage tool change so agent behavior does not silently shift.

capabilities.name: AI Developer Experience & Reuse Assets
capabilities.definition: Able to make the compliant path the easiest path for delivery teams.
sources: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture

criteria.name: Reference Implementation & Template Provision
criteria.definition: Publish working templates that already embed required controls.

criteria.name: SDK, Library & Component Curation
criteria.definition: Curate the approved libraries and shared components teams should build on.

criteria.name: Self-Service Onboarding
criteria.definition: Let a team start correctly without a bespoke engagement.

criteria.name: Inner-Source & Asset Reuse
criteria.definition: Make internally built assets discoverable and reusable across the institution.

criteria.name: Developer Documentation & Support
criteria.definition: Document the platform to the standard its users actually need.

capabilities.name: AI Deployment & Serving Operations
capabilities.definition: Able to place AI systems into production and keep them serving.

criteria.name: Model & Agent Deployment
criteria.definition: Deploy models and agents into production through a controlled mechanism.

criteria.name: Inference Serving & Scaling
criteria.definition: Serve inference at required throughput and scale it with demand.

criteria.name: Configuration & Feature Flag Control
criteria.definition: Change runtime behavior safely without redeployment.

criteria.name: System Availability & Continuity Management
criteria.definition: Meet availability and continuity commitments for individual AI systems in production.

criteria.name: Operational Readiness & Handover
criteria.definition: Hand over to operations with documented procedures before go-live.

capabilities.name: AI Monitoring & Observability
capabilities.definition: Able to see what an AI system did, in enough detail to explain it afterwards.

criteria.name: Telemetry Instrumentation & Collection
criteria.definition: Instrument AI systems to emit the signals operations and assurance need.

criteria.name: Trace & Interaction Logging
criteria.definition: Record prompts, context, outputs and decisions to a defined retention standard.

criteria.name: Agent Action & Tool-Call Observability
criteria.definition: See every action an agent took, with what arguments and to what effect.

criteria.name: Alerting & Threshold Management
criteria.definition: Detect abnormal behavior and raise it to someone who can act.

criteria.name: Operational Dashboarding
criteria.definition: Present operational state to the people accountable for it.

capabilities.name: Continuous Evaluation, Drift & Quality Management
capabilities.definition: Able to know that a system still performs as it did at release.

criteria.name: Production Output Quality Monitoring
criteria.definition: Measure output quality on live traffic, not only on test sets.

criteria.name: Data & Concept Drift Detection
criteria.definition: Detect when inputs or the world have moved away from training conditions.

criteria.name: Bias & Fairness Monitoring in Production
criteria.definition: Monitor outcome disparities on live populations over time.

criteria.name: Feedback Capture & Ground-Truth Collection
criteria.definition: Capture corrections and outcomes to build evolving ground truth.

criteria.name: Retraining & Refresh Triggering
criteria.definition: Trigger retraining or refresh on defined conditions rather than on schedule alone.

capabilities.name: AI Incident & Problem Management
capabilities.definition: Able to stop AI harm quickly and account for it afterwards.

criteria.name: AI Incident Detection & Classification
criteria.definition: Recognise an AI incident as distinct from a conventional IT incident.

criteria.name: Containment & Kill-Switch Execution
criteria.definition: Stop a model or agent immediately, at any hour, with a tested mechanism.

criteria.name: Root Cause Analysis
criteria.definition: Establish why an AI system behaved as it did, including at the data and prompt level.

criteria.name: Regulatory & Stakeholder Notification
criteria.definition: Notify the parties an incident obliges the institution to notify, within the deadline.

criteria.name: Corrective Action & Lessons Learned
criteria.definition: Close findings and feed them back into design and control.

capabilities.name: AI Cost Management
capabilities.definition: Able to know what AI costs, per unit of value, and to control it.
sources: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for AI

criteria.name: Consumption Metering & Attribution
criteria.definition: Attribute token, compute and storage consumption to an owner.

criteria.name: Cost Forecasting & Budget Control
criteria.definition: Forecast AI spend and stop it exceeding authorization.

criteria.name: Unit Economics & Cost-per-Outcome
criteria.definition: Express cost per transaction, per document or per outcome, not per month.

criteria.name: Optimization & Rightsizing
criteria.definition: Reduce cost through model, caching and routing choices without losing quality.

capabilities.name: AI Asset Retirement & Evidence Preservation
capabilities.definition: Able to retire AI systems deliberately, with their evidence preserved.

criteria.name: Periodic Recertification & Review
criteria.definition: Re-confirm at defined intervals that a system should remain in service.

criteria.name: Deprecation & Sunset Planning
criteria.definition: Plan and communicate withdrawal before it happens.

criteria.name: Decommissioning & Data Disposition
criteria.definition: Remove the system and dispose of its data under retention rules.

criteria.name: Archive & Evidence Preservation
criteria.definition: Preserve the records that assurance and legal obligations require after retirement.

capabilities.name: AI Policy, Standards & Management System
capabilities.definition: Able to operate a functioning management system for AI, not a policy document.

criteria.name: AI Management System Operation
criteria.definition: Operate the AIMS itself — scope, objectives, reviews, continual improvement.

criteria.name: AI Policy Development & Maintenance
criteria.definition: Issue and maintain the institutional AI policy set.

criteria.name: Standards & Technical Guideline Issuance
criteria.definition: Translate policy into standards a delivery team can actually build to.

criteria.name: Governance Body & Decision Rights Operation
criteria.definition: Run the forums that decide AI matters, with defined authority.

criteria.name: Exception & Dispensation Management
criteria.definition: Grant, time-box and track departures from standard.

criteria.name: Conformance Monitoring
criteria.definition: Detect where practice has diverged from policy without waiting for audit.

capabilities.name: Responsible & Trustworthy AI Practice
capabilities.definition: Able to make the institution's stated AI principles operative in delivered systems.

criteria.name: Fairness Standard Setting & Adjudication
criteria.definition: Set the fairness standard per use case, adjudicate measured disparity against it, and mandate remediation. Measurement is 6.3.3.

criteria.name: Transparency & Explainability Provision
criteria.definition: Provide explanation proportionate to the decision's consequence.

criteria.name: Human Agency & Oversight Enforcement
criteria.definition: Verify that designed oversight is actually exercised in operation.

criteria.name: Contestability & Redress Handling
criteria.definition: Give affected people a route to challenge an AI-influenced outcome.

criteria.name: Environmental & Social Responsibility
criteria.definition: Account for the environmental and social footprint of AI use.

capabilities.name: AI Risk Management
capabilities.definition: Able to identify, treat and monitor AI risk within a stated appetite.

criteria.name: AI Risk Identification & Taxonomy
criteria.definition: Maintain a common taxonomy of AI risks the institution recognizes.

criteria.name: Risk Assessment & Scoring
criteria.definition: Assess AI risks consistently enough to compare them across the portfolio.

criteria.name: Control Design & Treatment Planning
criteria.definition: Design proportionate controls and record accepted residual risk.

criteria.name: Risk Appetite & Tolerance Setting
criteria.definition: State how much AI risk the institution will carry, by category.

criteria.name: Risk Monitoring & Reporting
criteria.definition: Track risk position over time and report it to accountable bodies.

criteria.name: Independent Model Risk Validation
criteria.definition: Validate consequential models independently of the team that built them.

capabilities.name: AI Security & Resilience
capabilities.definition: Able to defend AI systems against attack, including attacks that use the AI itself.

criteria.name: AI Threat Modeling
criteria.definition: Model threats specific to AI systems, not only to their hosting infrastructure.

criteria.name: Model & Supply Chain Integrity
criteria.definition: Verify the provenance and integrity of models, weights and dependencies.

criteria.name: Injection & Jailbreak Detection and Response
criteria.definition: Detect subversion attempts in live traffic and respond to them.

criteria.name: Agent Identity & Credential Lifecycle
criteria.definition: Issue, sponsor, rotate and revoke a distinct identity per agent, rather than a shared service account.

criteria.name: Runtime Authorization & Action Control
criteria.definition: Authorise each consequential action at the moment it is attempted.

criteria.name: Output Filtering & Content Safety
criteria.definition: Prevent unsafe or disclosing output from reaching its recipient.

criteria.name: Adversarial & Red-Team Testing
criteria.definition: Actively attempt to make AI systems fail or misbehave, before release and on a recurring basis thereafter.

capabilities.name: Privacy & Data Protection for AI
capabilities.definition: Able to use personal data in AI without breaching the institution's obligations.

criteria.name: Privacy Impact Assessment for AI
criteria.definition: Assess privacy impact where AI processing introduces new exposure.

criteria.name: Personal Data Minimization & Masking
criteria.definition: Reduce personal data to what the purpose requires before it reaches a model.

criteria.name: Data Subject Rights Handling
criteria.definition: Answer access, correction and objection requests where AI is involved.

criteria.name: Confidentiality & Non-Disclosure Control
criteria.definition: Prevent confidential material leaving through model providers or outputs.

criteria.name: Training-Data Privacy Controls
criteria.definition: Control whether institutional data may be used to train provider models.

capabilities.name: Legal, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance for AI
capabilities.definition: Able to know which obligations bind the institution and to demonstrate compliance.

criteria.name: Regulatory Horizon Monitoring
criteria.definition: Track AI regulation across the jurisdictions the institution operates in.

criteria.name: Applicability & Obligation Mapping
criteria.definition: Determine which obligations apply to which AI system, and record why.

criteria.name: Intellectual Property & Copyright Control
criteria.definition: Manage IP exposure in both training inputs and generated outputs.

criteria.name: Records, Disclosure & Registration Obligations
criteria.definition: Meet registration, logging and disclosure duties on time.

criteria.name: Institutional Legal Status Determination
criteria.definition: Determine, as a prerequisite to any obligation mapping, how the institution's international legal status affects which AI regimes apply. Not a maturity dimension — a legal determination that exists or does not.

criteria.name: Regulatory Role Determination
criteria.definition: Establish whether the institution acts as provider, deployer or distributor for each AI system, as the prerequisite to obligation mapping.

capabilities.name: AI System & Agent Inventory Management
capabilities.definition: Able to state, at any moment, every AI system and agent in operation and who owns it.

criteria.name: AI System Registration
criteria.definition: Register every AI system before it reaches production, with mandatory attributes.

criteria.name: Agent Registration & Attribute Recording
criteria.definition: Record each agent in the inventory with its owner, purpose, scope and identity reference.

criteria.name: Ownership & Accountability Recording
criteria.definition: Record a named accountable individual for every registered AI system and keep it current as people and teams change.

criteria.name: Shadow AI Discovery
criteria.definition: Find AI in use that was never registered.

criteria.name: Inventory Completeness Assurance
criteria.definition: Test that the inventory is actually complete rather than assumed to be.

capabilities.name: AI Assurance & Evidence Management
capabilities.definition: Able to produce and retain evidence about AI that an independent reviewer can rely on. Independent assessment of that evidence is Internal Audit's, not this capability's.

criteria.name: Control Testing & Assurance Planning
criteria.definition: Plan and perform first- and second-line testing of AI controls on a risk basis.

criteria.name: Evidence Management & Audit Trail
criteria.definition: Retain evidence in a form an auditor can rely on, without reconstruction.

criteria.name: External Certification & Attestation
criteria.definition: Obtain and maintain external certification where it is required or valuable.

criteria.name: Finding Remediation Tracking
criteria.definition: Close audit and assurance findings and evidence the closure.

capabilities.name: AI Impact Assessment & Risk Classification
capabilities.definition: Able to determine, independently of the team proposing a use case, what impact it may have and what risk tier it belongs to.

criteria.name: AI System Impact Assessment
criteria.definition: Conduct the structured impact assessment on affected individuals and groups per ISO/IEC 42005.

criteria.name: Rights Impact Assessment Determination
criteria.definition: Determine whether a fundamental-rights impact assessment is required for a use case, and conduct it where it is.

criteria.name: Risk Classification & Tiering
criteria.definition: Assign each use case to a risk tier that determines the controls it must carry.

criteria.name: Classification Review & Reclassification
criteria.definition: Re-examine impact and risk tier when purpose, data, autonomy or affected population materially change.

criteria.name: Independent Challenge of First-Line Classification
criteria.definition: Challenge and, where warranted, overturn a proposing team's own assessment of impact or risk tier.

capabilities.name: AI Operating Model & Decision Rights
capabilities.definition: Able to say who decides what about AI, and who does the work.

criteria.name: Operating Model Design
criteria.definition: Choose and maintain the centralized, federated or hybrid model for AI work.

criteria.name: Role & Responsibility Definition
criteria.definition: Define the AI roles the institution needs and what each is accountable for.

criteria.name: Decision Rights & Escalation Paths
criteria.definition: State who may decide what, and where a disagreement goes.

criteria.name: Capacity & Resourcing Management
criteria.definition: Match available skilled capacity to the committed portfolio.

capabilities.name: AI Skills & Specialist Capability Building
capabilities.definition: Able to grow and retain the specialist skill the portfolio depends on.

criteria.name: Skills Taxonomy & Assessment
criteria.definition: Define the AI skills required and assess where the institution stands.

criteria.name: Training & Certification Delivery
criteria.definition: Deliver structured learning against identified gaps.

criteria.name: Recruitment & Talent Acquisition
criteria.definition: Acquire skills the institution cannot build in time.

criteria.name: Career Pathways & Retention
criteria.definition: Give AI practitioners a reason to stay.

capabilities.name: AI Literacy & Awareness
capabilities.definition: Able to ensure everyone who uses or is affected by AI understands enough to act safely.

criteria.name: Baseline AI Literacy Delivery
criteria.definition: Deliver a common minimum level of AI understanding across the institution.

criteria.name: Role-Specific Awareness
criteria.definition: Give each role the specific understanding its AI exposure requires.

criteria.name: Acceptable Use Communication
criteria.definition: Make clear, in practical terms, what staff may and may not do with AI.

criteria.name: Literacy Coverage Evidence
criteria.definition: Evidence who has received what AI training, to the standard the institution's own policy sets.

capabilities.name: AI Adoption, Enablement & Support
capabilities.definition: Able to convert delivered AI capability into actual, sustained use.

criteria.name: Adoption Planning & Targeting
criteria.definition: Plan adoption deliberately rather than assuming availability creates use.

criteria.name: User Onboarding & Enablement
criteria.definition: Bring new users to competent use quickly.

criteria.name: User Support Provision
criteria.definition: Answer users when AI behaves unexpectedly.

criteria.name: Adoption Measurement
criteria.definition: Measure real usage and depth of use, not licenses issued.

criteria.name: Champion Network Operation
criteria.definition: Sustain distributed advocates who carry adoption locally.

capabilities.name: AI Change Management & Workforce Transition
capabilities.definition: Able to carry the workforce through the change AI causes.

criteria.name: Change Impact Assessment
criteria.definition: Assess what AI changes for specific roles and teams before it lands.

criteria.name: Stakeholder Engagement & Communication
criteria.definition: Engage those affected early enough to influence the design.

criteria.name: Workforce Transition & Redeployment
criteria.definition: Move people whose work changes into work that is needed.

criteria.name: Staff Consultation & Representation
criteria.definition: Consult staff representation where AI changes conditions of work.

criteria.name: Trust & Resistance Management
criteria.definition: Address well-founded concern rather than treating it as an obstacle.

capabilities.name: AI Community & Reuse Culture
capabilities.definition: Able to make institutional learning about AI compound rather than repeat.
sources: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture

criteria.name: Practitioner Community Operation
criteria.definition: Sustain a working community across organizational boundaries.

criteria.name: Knowledge Sharing & Documentation
criteria.definition: Capture what was learned in a form others can find and use.

criteria.name: Reuse Incentives & Recognition
criteria.definition: Make reuse and contribution visibly worth doing.
